name: HunyuanVideo 1.5
summary: Tencent's 8.3B text-to-video model, 480p checkpoint, trained for 848×480 (16:9) at 121 frames and 24 fps. Newer and lighter than HunyuanVideo 1.0. Large download: NF4 quantization is on by default so the denoiser and the 7B text encoder fit a 16 GB card. Runs through the generic diffusers adapter; not yet tested end to end by Reel.
vram_note: Tencent's README: minimum 14 GB with model offloading. With NF4 here the denoiser is ~5 GB, but system RAM matters too: about 20 GB at the defaults. The repo stores the denoiser and VAE in fp32, which is why the download is larger than the loaded model.

native.note: Sizes are the 480p aspect-ratio buckets diffusers derives from the checkpoint's target size (640): about 0.41 megapixels, multiples of 16. Frames are 4n+1; the model card and README use 121 (5 s) at 24 fps, 50 steps, CFG 6.

unlock.note: The pipeline accepts any multiple of 16. This 480p checkpoint is trained for ~0.41 MP, so larger sizes are unlikely to look better; the 720p checkpoint reaches 1280×720. Tencent's report mentions 10-second clips (241 frames at 24 fps); no hard maximum is published.

memory.attention_note: Auto follows the diffusers docs: H100/H800 _flash_3_hub, A100/A800/RTX 4090 flash_hub, other GPUs sage_hub. They download a prebuilt kernel on first use. If one cannot load here (no build for your Windows / PyTorch / CUDA, or an untrusted publisher such as sage_hub's), Reel logs why and uses PyTorch's native attention.
memory.notes: Quantization applies to the 8.3B denoiser and the Qwen2.5-VL text encoder. Without it the loaded model is about 34 GB, which does not fit a 16 GB card and uses up a 32 GB PC's RAM.
